o1.biggest_strength: It correctly rejects the ₹1.86 crore draft, prioritises the top 5 matte shades, re-cartons held stock first, and keeps the PO plan inside the ₹1.2 crore cash limit.
o1.biggest_mistake: It assumes the 3,900 held top-5 units are already inside the 9,100 on hand, so it creates a false 1–8 December stockout gap instead of showing re-cartoning lifts top-5 stock to about 13,000 units and bridges to the rush delivery.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Fix the held-stock treatment, tighten the top-5 arrival/runout dates, and leave a little more cash buffer while keeping the same Monday action plan.

o2.biggest_strength: It gives a Monday-ready order plan with exact units, costs, dates, owners, cash held back, and clear no-order decisions for liquid lipstick, slow matte shades and glitter palettes.
o2.biggest_mistake: Like output 1, it treats the held top-5 units as part of the 9,100 on hand, which understates available stock after re-cartoning and invents a one-week top-shade stockout.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Correct the re-cartoning math so top-5 stock becomes 13,000 units, remove the unnecessary stockout/pre-order assumption, and adjust the date table accordingly.

reason: I would rather pay for output 2 because it is more operationally ready: it has cleaner cash control, owners, weekly checks and a useful reserve for rush upgrades. Both make the same important held-stock assumption error, so the win is only slight.
